title: Over Half of Gen Z Plan to Job Hunt in 2026
paragraphs: Young workers in the US are ready for a change. According to a new survey, more than half of Gen Z professionals plan to look for a new job before the end of 2026.

The survey was carried out by Robert Half, a recruitment and consulting company. It found that 55% of Gen Z professionals plan to start a job search before the end of the year. That is a big increase from one year ago, when only 32% said the same.
Money seems to be one of the biggest reasons. More than half of the young workers, 53%, believe that changing employers could help them earn more.

Among those who plan to look for a new job, 56% said they want better perks and benefits. Half said they do not have enough chances to move up in their current role. In addition, 37% said they were worried about keeping their artificial intelligence (AI) skills up to date.

When young people consider a job offer, benefits are very important to them. Health insurance was the top benefit, chosen by 65% of respondents. It was followed by flexible work schedules at 60% and help with travel costs at 57%.

AI is also creating some stress for young workers. Around 87% use AI for work, but 24% said using AI every day had caused them to experience burnout. Many said they felt pressure to be more productive, while others were afraid of losing their jobs if they did not use new tools.

Dawn Fay, an executive at Robert Half, said young professionals are taking a proactive approach to their careers. Fay added that employers should be clear about career growth, pay and support if they want to keep their workers. According to Fay, companies can help by offering practical training that builds confidence without adding to burnout.
